title: A review is a pull request's slide deck
statement: A review is equivalent to a pull request and is always a slide deck that explains what the change did and why, so a reviewer can be confident the deck explains every line.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A review's base is the pull request's base, its head follows the pull request as commits are pushed, and there is one review per pull request.

The review deck explains the transition and its reasoning that the current state no longer shows; its Items reference commits and may reference Saga records such as the story or epic slide a change revises.
Each review slide records its state (approved, changes requested, or none) with the head commit it was given at, and comments attach to review slides and Items.
An approval is out of date when the slide, or the code it references, changed between that commit and the pull request's current head.
Every changed line in the review's range must be covered by the review deck's Items; coverage is reported per review, with covered, uncovered, and stale lines and the uncovered lines listed.
The tool never declares a review approved; status and check report every slide's state and currency, and the team decides what it requires.
After merge the review is history, and a node's history links to the reviews that changed it.
